Applications

Apps provide simple access to information and tools for citizens to understand your community. We recommend exploring the apps below for helping engage around specific goals and initiatives - as well as encourage people to create their own stories and apps using the API and ready to configure apps.



  • Local Perspective


    Configure apps to provide focused citizen experiences.



  • Story Maps



    Tell stories about local issues and solutions.



  • Survey 123



    Hear from your community.



  • Open Data



    Make your data discoverable, explorable and usable.


Explore More Apps

Unlock the Data

Anyone can use open data from the Government Open Data at no cost. Download raw data and share your insights with your community or build new applications that serve specific users.

Explore

Dig into the data.

Visualize & Analyze

Highlight spatial patterns and discover trends.

Build

Develop new apps using templates and API's.

Share

Embed analysis on your website.

Local Narratives

Everyone has a story to tell. Engage and inspire your audience by combining text, images, and other multimedia content with maps. You have the local knowledge and expertise, now begin and sustain a meaningful connection with your users.

Learn More

• Story Maps



    Share local knowledge and insights.

• ArcGIS for Developers


    Develop new Apps and Solutions for your Community.

Open API

Use an Open Platform to spur innovation and stay on top of the latest technology. Utilizing open standards, interoperability, data, APIs, and code can connect you directly to the community.

Our Open Vision | Developer API

Community Events

Open Data is best used in coordination between citizens, businesses, and government. By hosting meetups and in-person events you can share knowledge and build a cohesive collaboration to solve your more important initiatives. It is often helpful to have regular and on-going events that align with existing local community events when possible.

Examples:

  • GeoDev Meetup on visualization
  • Transportation Data Meetup, hosted by DOT
  • Public Safety and You, hosted by PD
  • Community App Challenge, hosted by Mayor's office
  • ConnectEd event with local Schools

https://www.arcgis.com/sharing/rest/cont.description:
The City of Cornwall has a rich and diverse history spanning well over 230 years, which includes many colonial, industrial, economic, and cultural influences.


Cornwall's heritage is a source of strength and confidence that puts the changes of society into perspective and pushes us to grow and strive for a greater community. The City's historic legacy is embodied in the form of its works, institutions, monuments, and buildings; which are worthy of protection so that they may be shared with future generations.


The Ontario Heritage Act and its initiatives help to foster a sense of pride while promoting culture as both a valuable source of knowledge, as well as a central element of a healthy community. Section 27 of the Ontario Heritage Act requires every municipality to maintain a current, publicly accessible register of properties of cultural heritage value or interest by way of a resolution of council.


The Municipal Register is an official list or record of cultural heritage properties that have been identified as being important to the community. This initiative is in line with the Ontario Provincial Policy Statement's vision for protecting valuable resources, including heritage resources, as well as the City of Cornwall's Official Plan which has outlined provisions for protecting heritage resources.
